items.title: NERAI Maritime Weekly
events: FOLLOW-UP - Hormuz Blockade: 4-Week Risk Falls 6.8 pts Even as Oil Flow Stays at -96.4% — Divergence Persists
Oman-Mediated Hormuz Talks: Technical Framework Agreed, No Signed Deal Yet
FOLLOW-UP - Saudi East-West Pipeline Struck Again — Last Hormuz Bypass Remains Disabled
FOLLOW-UP - Houthis Consolidate Bab el-Mandeb Control: Mocha Port, Perim Island Held; IRGC Officers Deployed
Iranian Commercial Vessel Struck Near Qeshm; Iran Attributes Attack to U.S., 1 Killed, 3 Injured
items.summary: The Gulf crisis deepened materially this week as Hormuz physical oil flow remained at -96.4% versus baseline while NERAI's 4-week disruption probability fell 6.8 points to 44% — a sustained divergence between the forward model and the water that warrants close monitoring. Simultaneously, Houthi consolidation of Bab el-Mandeb accelerated, closing the Cape-of-Good-Hope reroute valve from the Red Sea side, and the Saudi East-West pipeline sustained a second alleged strike, eliminating the last credible overland Hormuz bypass. Diplomatic activity in Muscat produced a technical framework on Hormuz transit lanes but no signed agreement, leaving the strategic picture unresolved heading into next week.
